findings.title: Reschedule path cancels via SendGrid immediately, bringing back the 100-pending-cancellation failure
findings.body: The PR moves normal cancellations to a deferred model: set `cancelled = true`, and let the cron cancel in SendGrid within an hour of the send time. This was meant to avoid SendGrid's cap of about 100 pending cancellations. The reschedule path in handleNewBooking passes `immediateDelete = true`, so each rescheduled booking sends a cancel request to SendGrid right away. Once the cap is reached, the request fails and the error is only logged. The row is neither marked `cancelled` nor deleted, so the cron never retries and the reminder email for the old time is still sent. That is the bug this PR set out to fix. The same reminders are also cancelled a second time when the booking was first cancelled through `requestReschedule` (which already flagged them `cancelled`), which uses up another pending-cancel slot. The reschedule path should use the deferred flag, as `requestReschedule` and `handleCancelBooking` do.

findings.title: immediateDelete branch swallows SendGrid errors and never records the cancellation
findings.body: In the `immediateDelete` branch the function POSTs the cancel to SendGrid and returns. It neither deletes the reminder row nor sets `cancelled`. If the request fails (for example at the 100 pending-cancellation limit), the outer catch only logs, so there is no fallback and the cron cannot retry. If the request succeeds, the row lingers until the scheduled date passes. This only works for callers whose rows are cascade-deleted afterwards (workflow or step deletion). For callers whose rows persist, such as the reschedule path, a failed cancel is lost. The branch should fall back to flagging `cancelled` on failure, or callers whose rows persist should not use it.

findings.title: One failing SendGrid cancel aborts the whole batch and blocks later cancellations on every run
findings.body: The cancel loop sits in a single try/catch. The `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` calls are lazy PrismaPromises that only run at `await Promise.all(...)` after the loop. If any `client.request` throws (invalid or expired batch_id, rate limit, transient error), the loop exits and none of the deletes run, including those for reminders already cancelled. Reminders after the failing one are never processed. The failing row is still `cancelled: true` with a date inside the next hour, so it is retried first on every 15-minute run and fails again. All later cancelled reminders then go out as emails. Each reminder should be handled in its own try/catch, and its row deleted right after its own successful cancel.

findings.title: Shared @sendgrid/client is never given the API key in this module, so the new cancel calls may be unauthenticated
findings.body: This file only calls `sgMail.setApiKey(...)`. `@sendgrid/mail` uses its own internal Client instance, so that does not configure the default `@sendgrid/client` singleton used for `client.request`. Nothing in this module calls `client.setApiKey`. The new cancellation loop depends entirely on `client.request`. If the singleton has no key in the cron's process, every cancel returns 401. That error is swallowed by the try/catch (`console.log`), so nothing is cancelled and the emails still go out, silently. Add `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` here, as emailReminderManager does.

findings.title: Unused `Prisma` import and type imports turned into value imports
findings.body: After the `PrismaPromise<Prisma.BatchPayload>[]` code was removed, `Prisma` is no longer used in this file, so it is an unused import (a lint failure). `PrismaPromise` was also changed from `import type` to a regular value import even though it is only used as a type. The same pattern appears in handleNewBooking.ts, where `App`, `Credential`, `EventTypeCustomInput` and `Prisma` were moved from `import type` to a value import. Restore the type-only imports and drop `Prisma`.

findings.title: No tests for the new deferred-cancellation flow
findings.body: The fix changes the contract of `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` and adds a new cron phase. It also rewires cancel, reschedule, workflow-update and workflow-delete paths. No tests were added for any of it: setting `cancelled`, the one-hour cancellation window, deleting rows after a successful cancel, or behaviour when SendGrid fails. The earlier fix in #6991 had to be redone because it was never exercised against SendGrid's real limits, so regression coverage matters here.
